newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says not concerned US economy will overheat.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says not concerned US economy will overheat.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said he is not worried about the U.S. economy overheating and reiterated his belief that a strong dollar is in the nation's best interests.

When asked if strong Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in recent quarters has caused him concern about prospects for a too-strong economy, Rubin said, "No. ... Basically, I think we are on a very good track. ... I think the most likely scenario is we'll continue on a track of solid growth and low inflation."
Rubin said market interest rates rise during periods of strong growth, helping to keep GDP in check.

When asked if interest rates would have been higher without the strong recent inflow of foreign capital, Rubin said, "Sure. By attracting foreign capital, you tend to keep interest rates lower. And that, by the way, is another reason why a strong dollar has worked to our interests."
The Treasury Secretary repeated that even though he favored a strong dollar, he shared Japan's concern about the weakness of the yen.
Rubin said U.S. consumers' debt burdens are not a threat to economic growth.
"Two sets of economists I have asked that question to do not think consumer debt at current levels posed a material risk to the economy," he said.
Turning to the Treasury's inflation-protected securities, Rubin said he did not think the new notes would raise the government's borrowing costs.

"By putting this in our debt structure at an appropriate place in the yield curve ..., I think if you compare it to the fixed-rate debt that it will replace, on balance ... it will actually lower our cost of money," he said.
